observation.visible_scene: A static nighttime shot of a fireworks display over a dark horizon line with scattered ground lights and a low bank of illuminated smoke. A large overlapping cluster of bursts fills the upper two-thirds of the frame: an orange-red spherical burst on the left, a magenta/purple spherical burst at the top right, a green burst at top center, a bright pink mass in the middle, a green burst at mid-right, and a small orange burst at lower left. Several smaller white/gold 'peony' shells are embedded in the cluster.
visible_changes: The overall burst cluster drifts slowly upward relative to the fixed smoke and horizon lights (the orange-red sphere moves from mid-frame toward the top).

New distinct spherical peony bursts emerge and expand during the segment: an orange-white peony on the left grows from a faint point (~frame 12) into a full sphere (~frame 30), a white peony on the right enlarges, and a red-gold peony appears at the top right (~frame 17) and expands.
The central pink/red mass intensifies and shifts upward as its lower trails fade.
The small white burst near the center present at the start fades and is absorbed into the larger red sphere.
The smoke bank at the bottom persists throughout, with its lit color shifting between pink and pale yellow as the overhead bursts change.
outside_clip_unknowns: The launch and initial detonation of the shells that were already mid-expansion at frame 1.
The final fade-out and falling trails of the bursts after frame 40.
Whether additional shells are fired beyond the last sampled frame.
uncertain_details: The apparent upward drift of the red sphere may reflect physical rise of the burst or asymmetric fading of its lower trails; the camera itself is static.
It is not determinable from the frames whether the newly appearing peony spheres are separate shells or secondary bursts of the same shells.
Exact timing of individual burst onsets is approximate due to the sampling interval.
